scene.label: Act 4, Scene 4
scene.title: SCENE IV. Rome. Before the Palace

content.text: Enter Emperor Saturninus and Empress Tamora and her two sons Chiron and Demetrius, with Attendants. The Emperor brings the arrows in his hand that Titus shot at him.

lines.text: Why, lords, what wrongs are these! Was ever seen
lines.plainText: Why lords what wrongs are these Was ever seen

lines.text: An emperor in Rome thus overborne,
lines.plainText: An emperor in Rome thus overborne

lines.text: Troubled, confronted thus; and, for the extent
lines.plainText: Troubled confronted thus and for the extent

lines.text: Of legal justice, used in such contempt?
lines.plainText: Of legal justice used in such contempt

lines.text: My lords, you know, as know the mightful gods,
lines.plainText: My lords you know as know the mightful gods

lines.text: However these disturbers of our peace
lines.plainText: However these disturbers of our peace

lines.text: Buzz in the people's ears, there naught hath passed
lines.plainText: Buzz in the people's ears there naught hath passed

lines.text: But even with law against the wilful sons
lines.plainText: But even with law against the wilful sons

lines.text: Of old Andronicus. And what an if
lines.plainText: Of old Andronicus And what an if

lines.text: His sorrows have so overwhelmed his wits?
lines.plainText: His sorrows have so overwhelmed his wits

lines.text: Shall we be thus afflicted in his wreaks,
lines.plainText: Shall we be thus afflicted in his wreaks

lines.text: His fits, his frenzy, and his bitterness?
lines.plainText: His fits his frenzy and his bitterness

lines.text: And now he writes to heaven for his redress!
lines.plainText: And now he writes to heaven for his redress

lines.text: See, here's "to Jove," and this "to Mercury,"
lines.plainText: See here's to Jove and this to Mercury

lines.text: This "to Apollo," this to the god of war.
lines.plainText: This to Apollo this to the god of war

lines.text: Sweet scrolls to fly about the streets of Rome!
lines.plainText: Sweet scrolls to fly about the streets of Rome

lines.text: What's this but libelling against the senate,
lines.plainText: What's this but libelling against the senate

lines.text: And blazoning our injustice everywhere?
lines.plainText: And blazoning our injustice everywhere

lines.text: A goodly humour, is it not, my lords?
lines.plainText: A goodly humour is it not my lords

lines.text: As who would say, in Rome no justice were.
lines.plainText: As who would say in Rome no justice were

lines.text: But if I live, his feigned ecstasies
lines.plainText: But if I live his feigned ecstasies

lines.text: Shall be no shelter to these outrages;
lines.plainText: Shall be no shelter to these outrages

lines.text: But he and his shall know that justice lives
lines.plainText: But he and his shall know that justice lives

lines.text: In Saturninus' health; whom, if she sleep,
lines.plainText: In Saturninus' health whom if she sleep

lines.text: He'll so awake as he in fury shall
lines.plainText: He'll so awake as he in fury shall

lines.text: Cut off the proud'st conspirator that lives.
lines.plainText: Cut off the proud'st conspirator that lives

lines.text: My gracious lord, my lovely Saturnine,
lines.plainText: My gracious lord my lovely Saturnine

lines.text: Lord of my life, commander of my thoughts,
lines.plainText: Lord of my life commander of my thoughts

lines.text: Calm thee, and bear the faults of Titus' age,
lines.plainText: Calm thee and bear the faults of Titus' age

lines.text: Th' effects of sorrow for his valiant sons,
lines.plainText: Th' effects of sorrow for his valiant sons

lines.text: Whose loss hath pierced him deep and scarred his heart;
lines.plainText: Whose loss hath pierced him deep and scarred his heart

lines.text: And rather comfort his distressed plight
lines.plainText: And rather comfort his distressed plight

lines.text: Than prosecute the meanest or the best
lines.plainText: Than prosecute the meanest or the best

lines.text: For these contempts. [Aside.] Why, thus it shall become
lines.plainText: For these contempts Aside Why thus it shall become

lines.text: High-witted Tamora to gloze with all.
lines.plainText: Highwitted Tamora to gloze with all

lines.text: But, Titus, I have touched thee to the quick;
lines.plainText: But Titus I have touched thee to the quick

lines.text: Thy life-blood out, if Aaron now be wise,
lines.plainText: Thy lifeblood out if Aaron now be wise

lines.text: Then is all safe, the anchor in the port.
lines.plainText: Then is all safe the anchor in the port

lines.text: Yes, forsooth, an your mistresship be emperial.
lines.plainText: Yes forsooth an your mistresship be emperial

lines.text: Empress I am, but yonder sits the emperor.
lines.plainText: Empress I am but yonder sits the emperor

lines.text: 'Tis he. God and Saint Stephen give you good e'en. I have brought you a letter and a couple of pigeons here.
lines.plainText: 'Tis he God and Saint Stephen give you good e'en I have brought you a letter and a couple of pigeons here

lines.text: Go take him away, and hang him presently.
lines.plainText: Go take him away and hang him presently

lines.text: How much money must I have?
lines.plainText: How much money must I have

lines.text: Come, sirrah, you must be hanged.
lines.plainText: Come sirrah you must be hanged

lines.text: Hanged! by'r Lady, then I have brought up a neck to a fair end.
lines.plainText: Hanged by'r Lady then I have brought up a neck to a fair end

lines.text: Despiteful and intolerable wrongs!
lines.plainText: Despiteful and intolerable wrongs

lines.text: Shall I endure this monstrous villainy?
lines.plainText: Shall I endure this monstrous villainy

lines.text: I know from whence this same device proceeds.
lines.plainText: I know from whence this same device proceeds

lines.text: May this be borne as if his traitorous sons,
lines.plainText: May this be borne as if his traitorous sons

lines.text: That died by law for murder of our brother,
lines.plainText: That died by law for murder of our brother

lines.text: Have by my means been butchered wrongfully?
lines.plainText: Have by my means been butchered wrongfully

lines.text: Go, drag the villain hither by the hair;
lines.plainText: Go drag the villain hither by the hair

lines.text: Nor age nor honour shall shape privilege.
lines.plainText: Nor age nor honour shall shape privilege

lines.text: For this proud mock I'll be thy slaughterman,
lines.plainText: For this proud mock I'll be thy slaughterman

lines.text: Sly frantic wretch, that holp'st to make me great,
lines.plainText: Sly frantic wretch that holp'st to make me great

lines.text: In hope thyself should govern Rome and me.
lines.plainText: In hope thyself should govern Rome and me

lines.text: Arm, my lord! Rome never had more cause.
lines.plainText: Arm my lord Rome never had more cause

lines.text: The Goths have gathered head, and with a power
lines.plainText: The Goths have gathered head and with a power

lines.text: Of high-resolved men, bent to the spoil,
lines.plainText: Of highresolved men bent to the spoil

lines.text: They hither march amain, under conduct
lines.plainText: They hither march amain under conduct

lines.text: Of Lucius, son to old Andronicus;
lines.plainText: Of Lucius son to old Andronicus

lines.text: Who threats, in course of this revenge, to do
lines.plainText: Who threats in course of this revenge to do

lines.text: As much as ever Coriolanus did.
lines.plainText: As much as ever Coriolanus did

lines.text: Is warlike Lucius general of the Goths?
lines.plainText: Is warlike Lucius general of the Goths

lines.text: These tidings nip me, and I hang the head
lines.plainText: These tidings nip me and I hang the head

lines.text: As flowers with frost, or grass beat down with storms.
lines.plainText: As flowers with frost or grass beat down with storms

lines.text: Ay, now begins our sorrows to approach.
lines.plainText: Ay now begins our sorrows to approach

lines.text: 'Tis he the common people love so much;
lines.plainText: 'Tis he the common people love so much

lines.text: Myself hath often overheard them say,
lines.plainText: Myself hath often overheard them say

lines.text: When I have walked like a private man,
lines.plainText: When I have walked like a private man

lines.text: That Lucius' banishment was wrongfully,
lines.plainText: That Lucius' banishment was wrongfully

lines.text: And they have wished that Lucius were their emperor.
lines.plainText: And they have wished that Lucius were their emperor

lines.text: Why should you fear? Is not your city strong?
lines.plainText: Why should you fear Is not your city strong

lines.text: Ay, but the citizens favour Lucius,
lines.plainText: Ay but the citizens favour Lucius

lines.text: And will revolt from me to succour him.
lines.plainText: And will revolt from me to succour him

lines.text: King, be thy thoughts imperious like thy name.
lines.plainText: King be thy thoughts imperious like thy name

lines.text: Is the sun dimmed, that gnats do fly in it?
lines.plainText: Is the sun dimmed that gnats do fly in it

lines.text: The eagle suffers little birds to sing,
lines.plainText: The eagle suffers little birds to sing

lines.text: And is not careful what they mean thereby,
lines.plainText: And is not careful what they mean thereby

lines.text: Knowing that with the shadow of his wings
lines.plainText: Knowing that with the shadow of his wings

lines.text: He can at pleasure stint their melody;
lines.plainText: He can at pleasure stint their melody

lines.text: Even so mayest thou the giddy men of Rome.
lines.plainText: Even so mayest thou the giddy men of Rome

lines.text: Then cheer thy spirit; for know, thou emperor,
lines.plainText: Then cheer thy spirit for know thou emperor

lines.text: I will enchant the old Andronicus
lines.plainText: I will enchant the old Andronicus

lines.text: With words more sweet, and yet more dangerous,
lines.plainText: With words more sweet and yet more dangerous

lines.text: Than baits to fish or honey-stalks to sheep,
lines.plainText: Than baits to fish or honeystalks to sheep

lines.text: Whenas the one is wounded with the bait,
lines.plainText: Whenas the one is wounded with the bait

lines.text: The other rotted with delicious feed.
lines.plainText: The other rotted with delicious feed

lines.text: But he will not entreat his son for us.
lines.plainText: But he will not entreat his son for us

lines.text: If Tamora entreat him, then he will,
lines.plainText: If Tamora entreat him then he will

lines.text: For I can smooth and fill his aged ears
lines.plainText: For I can smooth and fill his aged ears

lines.text: With golden promises, that, were his heart
lines.plainText: With golden promises that were his heart

lines.text: Almost impregnable, his old ears deaf,
lines.plainText: Almost impregnable his old ears deaf

lines.text: Yet should both ear and heart obey my tongue.
lines.plainText: Yet should both ear and heart obey my tongue

lines.text: [to Aemilius] Go thou before, be our ambassador.
lines.plainText: to Aemilius Go thou before be our ambassador

lines.text: Say that the emperor requests a parley
lines.plainText: Say that the emperor requests a parley

lines.text: Of warlike Lucius, and appoint the meeting
lines.plainText: Of warlike Lucius and appoint the meeting

lines.text: Even at his father's house, the old Andronicus.
lines.plainText: Even at his father's house the old Andronicus

lines.text: Aemilius, do this message honourably,
lines.plainText: Aemilius do this message honourably

lines.text: And if he stand on hostage for his safety,
lines.plainText: And if he stand on hostage for his safety

lines.text: Bid him demand what pledge will please him best.
lines.plainText: Bid him demand what pledge will please him best

lines.text: Your bidding shall I do effectually.
lines.plainText: Your bidding shall I do effectually

lines.text: Now will I to that old Andronicus,
lines.plainText: Now will I to that old Andronicus

lines.text: And temper him with all the art I have,
lines.plainText: And temper him with all the art I have

lines.text: To pluck proud Lucius from the warlike Goths.
lines.plainText: To pluck proud Lucius from the warlike Goths

lines.text: And now, sweet emperor, be blithe again,
lines.plainText: And now sweet emperor be blithe again

lines.text: And bury all thy fear in my devices.
lines.plainText: And bury all thy fear in my devices

lines.text: Then go successantly, and plead to him.
lines.plainText: Then go successantly and plead to him
